definition: Small probe charges, often several within minutes at different (often digital) merchants, to check that a stolen card works; sometimes followed by a larger cash-out.

Someone else has taken over an ACTIVE customer's online account or card credentials: often a recent change of email, phone or password and a new device, then larger-than-usual online purchases, sometimes at unusual hours. If the card had been inactive for weeks before this, choose dormant_reactivation instead.
A cloned physical card used in person far from the customer's home, sometimes within hours of a genuine swipe at home (impossible travel).

A card that was inactive for weeks suddenly makes purchases, typically online, often from a new device and larger than usual. This takes precedence over account_takeover whenever the card had been inactive for weeks.
The evidence does not clearly fit one typology.
Cash deposits split into amounts just under the 10,000 USD reporting threshold, often across several branches, to avoid currency transaction reports.
Money arrives from many new counterparties and leaves again within hours, so almost nothing stays in the account; typical of money-mule accounts.
Repeated wires, often in round amounts, to jurisdictions with weak anti-money-laundering controls, out of line with the customer's profile.
An account that was inactive for most of the year suddenly moves large volumes.

A claim filed very soon after the policy started, as if the loss was planned before buying cover.
Accident claims whose parties also appear in other claims, with soft-tissue injuries and no police report; typical of organised rings.
A genuine loss claimed at a much higher amount than similar claims, often through a repair shop with a history of flagged claims.

Many failed logins against many different usernames from the same source, trying common passwords.
Unusually large outbound data transfers to a new external destination, often off-hours.
A host calling out to an external server at very regular intervals, as malware does to receive commands.
